key_insight: DFT-derived stacking-fault energy surfaces enable reliable PFDD predictions of stacking-fault widths in Cu–Al alloys, while surfaces from the tested classical and machine-learned potentials cause premature partial-dislocation pinning.
engineering_relevance: Accurate shear-energy landscapes are essential for multiscale models of alloy dislocation behavior, even when interatomic potentials reproduce lattice parameters and elastic moduli.
method: Compare generalized stacking-fault energy surfaces from DFT, a classical embedded-atom potential (ZW), and a machine-learned Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP).
Use each energy surface in phase-field dislocation dynamics (PFDD) to predict equilibrium stacking-fault widths across Al contents.
Assess predictions against standalone molecular dynamics results and experimental values for pure Cu.
evidence_signal: DFT-informed PFDD predicts increasing stacking-fault width with Al content and agrees well with standalone MD measurements and pure-Cu experiments; ZW and GAP surfaces deviate substantially from DFT at seven characteristic points, especially T and T₁.
watch_item: The findings concern the tested ZW and GAP potentials; reproducing bulk properties alone does not establish suitability for stacking-fault modeling.
paper_title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
